_instructions: Engineering design process description. 'steps' drives the cycle diagram. 'notebookPath' is a path to the PDF served from /public/.

steps.label: Ask
steps.description: Identify the need and constraints. Used our COB strategy at the start of the season to define priorities and guide game strategy decisions.

steps.label: Imagine
steps.description: Investigate the problem. Analyzed risks, constraints, and gameplay challenges to inform design decisions.

steps.label: Make a Plan
steps.description: Select a promising solution. Developed concepts using CAD and hand-drawn designs to evaluate potential solutions.

steps.label: Create
steps.description: Build a prototype. Built iterative prototypes beginning with cardboard, progressing to 3D-printed parts, and refining into final designs.

steps.label: Test
steps.description: Evaluate the prototype. Tested prototypes in game-like conditions to measure consistency, efficiency, and performance.

steps.label: Improve
steps.description: Redesign as needed. Refined designs through repeated iterations, using testing data to drive continuous improvement.

narrative: Having a detailed process allows us to sustain effective prototyping and testing periods. Each year we start with a COB strategy session — identifying what is Critical, Optional, and Bypass — to create a game strategy before touching any tools. Every decision, including ones we reject, is documented in the engineering notebook with the reasoning, giving us a traceable record and helping new members understand why the robot looks the way it does.
